title: Thyroid hormones (TSH, T4)
what: A blood test from a vein for hormones that show how your thyroid gland is working.
why: For tiredness, weight changes, a racing heart, hair loss, during pregnancy or when planning one, and to check treatment.
duration: the blood draw takes 3 to 5 minutes, and results usually take 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: If you take biotin or hair and nail vitamins. Biotin can change the result

prepare.title: Time
prepare.text: Morning is best, usually before 10 or 11. Repeat tests should be at about the same time.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually fasting, or a few hours after a light meal. Ask the lab. Water is fine.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. If you take thyroid hormone, ask your doctor whether to take it before or after the test.

prepare.title: Supplements
prepare.text: Tell your doctor about biotin in advance. You are often asked to stop it 2 to 3 days before the test, but the doctor decides.

bring: Past results and thyroid ultrasound reports, if you have them
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tied on your arm, and the skin is cleaned with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills the tube
The needle is removed, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
A doctor explains the result, usually a hormone specialist called an endocrinologist

faq.q: Do I need to fast for a TSH test?
faq.a: Not strictly, but it is best in the morning and at about the same time. That makes results easier to compare.

faq.q: Should I take my thyroid pill before the test?
faq.a: Ask your doctor. Often the pill is taken after the blood draw, so it does not change the result.
